records.title: Scenario 1, Task 1: Build a Meeting Room Booking System
records.summary: Built a working meeting room booking web app that replaces the shared spreadsheet. It is a single Python file (standard library only, no install) with a browser UI and a JSON data file. You asked me to use defaults, so it has 4 rooms (Aspen 4, Birch 6, Cedar 10, Dune 20), 30-minute slots 08:00–18:00 Mon–Fri, name required (no login), anyone can cancel, max 4 hours per booking, up to 60 days ahead, no buffer. What it does: - Check availability: pick a date and see a grid of all rooms x 30-min slots, green = free, red = booked with the meeting title and who booked it; plus a 'find a free room f…
records.judge_notes: The delivered app.py, test_app.py and README.md fully implement the requested booking system with all defaults, overlap rejection, immediate cancellation, my-bookings, recurring bookings, a lock, and a test script. The README gives the exact start command and a step-by-step usage walkthrough, and the final reply explains what was built and how to use it. The only caveat is that UI verification was HTTP-level rather than a real browser click-through, which the team disclosed.

records.title: Scenario 2, Task 1: Produce a News Report
records.summary: Produced the requested news report on AI on HKUST campuses, in English, for students and faculty, in three channel versions in one file: hkust_ai_report.md. Story chosen after consulting you (you approved the default): HKUST's generative-AI policy for teaching and learning — the course-by-course rule in force since Fall 2023-24 — plus the new six-credit AI and data literacy (HAIC) requirement for all undergraduates admitted from 2026-27, the free HKUST GenAI Platform with HKGAI V1 (22 Apr 2025), and the AI Literacy Hub announced 7 Nov 2025. Contents: (1) main article for the university news s…
records.judge_notes: The story choice, investigation, three-channel structure and 'why it matters' are all delivered, and the social post and bulletin are within length and self-contained. However, the main article is visibly well over the 900-word limit (the chief editor admits the final word count was never re-measured after edits, and the text runs to roughly 1,000+ words), so the explicit 700–900 word requirement is not met. The final version also never received a re-check after fact-check corrections, leaving some claims (e.g. Dr Jac Leung's directorship, the Senate approval date) unconfirmed.

records.title: Scenario 2, Task 2: Fact-Check AI-Writing Detectors
records.summary: Wrote the fact-check article ai_detector_factcheck.md (English, for students and faculty) on the claim "AI-writing detectors can reliably determine whether a university student's assignment was written by AI." Verdict: Mostly False — detectors give a signal for human review, not proof. You approved the defaults (strict reading of "reliably", Mostly False verdict, ~900–1,100 words, HKUST as the institutional example). The article covers: peer-reviewed testing (Weber-Wulff et al., IJEI, 25 Dec 2023: tools "neither accurate nor reliable"); bias against non-native English writers (Liang et al., P…
records.judge_notes: The article is substantive, well-sourced, correctly structured and covers every content requirement including HKUST and the uncertainty section; unverified figures are marked. However, the agreed 900–1,100-word body target was missed (~1,300 words), and the team itself reports that no reviewer re-checked the final corrected version, so verbatim accuracy of the final text rests on the chief editor's own corrections rather than independent verification.

records.title: Scenario 3, Task 2: The Future of the Semiconductor Industry: An HTML Slide Presentation
records.summary: Delivered an 11-slide, self-contained HTML deck (semiconductor_outlook_2026.html) for the fund team, written from an end-of-2026 perspective. You confirmed 'use all defaults' (internal fund team, full value chain, 2027-2030 horizon, English, sector-level views only). Structure: title/house view; 2026 in review (WSTS $1,655bn 2026, +108%; SOX -38.5% peak-to-trough, forward P/E 26.1x to ~13x on +155% EPS); AI compute demand and the 2027 ASIC-vs-GPU unit shift; memory/HBM4; supply bottleneck (TSMC, SEMI, ASML); policy/China (Section 232, remote-access rule, 10 Jan 2027 binary date, localisation)…
records.judge_notes: The deck is a real, self-contained, navigable HTML presentation with sourced judgments, investment implications and a risk table, so the core request is substantially delivered. However it falls short of the agreed ~14–16 slides (11 delivered), several slides overflow and scroll inside the card, and the team's own fact-check, risk and marketing reviews all returned FAIL with numerous unresolved accuracy, sourcing and consistency issues (mixed as-of dates, single-aggregator drawdown table, some UNVERIFIED items still presented as fact). The final reply candidly states the review was not cleared
